questions.question: What does setting include?
choices: the time and place of a story

questions.question: Tone is best defined as the author’s or narrator’s what toward the subject?
Mood refers most directly to the feeling a text creates in the what?
“By dawn, the empty station smelled of rain and cold metal.” Which element is most directly established?
“The mayor’s ‘brilliant plan’ left the town without water,” the narrator says. What tone is suggested?
A quiet path, fading light, and distant footsteps create an uneasy feeling. What is being built?
A story shifts from a crowded city street to an isolated cabin. What changes most directly?
A narrator describes a storm as “a welcome guest that rinsed the dusty fields.” What tone is suggested?
An author uses clipped sentences and harsh words to describe a failed plan. Which inference is strongest?
“Lanterns glowed in the windows while music drifted across the square.” What mood is most strongly created?
A scene occurs during a drought, but characters speak with humor and hope. Which statement distinguishes the elements?
choices: tone and setting mean the same thing
setting is harsh while tone may remain hopeful
setting is determined by dialogue only

questions.question: A writer wants a suspenseful mood. Which detail best supports that purpose?
choices: birds sing above a sunny garden
a child laughs at a familiar joke
a latch clicks behind the character in an otherwise silent hall

questions.question: A narrator calls a difficult journey “a pleasant little stroll” while describing blisters and exhaustion. What tone is most likely?
Readers feel sympathy during a scene, though the narrator’s language stays factual. Which idea explains this?
choices: setting is the same as mood
tone is always an emotion in the reader

questions.question: A story set in a school during a blackout uses flickering lights and empty corridors. What combination chiefly creates unease?
An author describes a character’s home warmly but the surrounding town critically. What can change within one scene?
choices: tone can shift with the narrator’s focus
point of view must become first person

questions.question: A bleak landscape is described in playful, exaggerated language. Which conclusion is defensible?
choices: the setting may be bleak while the tone is playful
the mood is certainly bleak for every reader

questions.question: A character returns to a familiar room after many years; the room is smaller than remembered. What can the setting detail suggest?
choices: the story has no time period

questions.question: Which revision would create a more hopeful mood in a scene about a storm?
choices: neighbors bring lanterns and food to the shelter
the roof groans under another gust
the lights fail one by one

questions.question: Two readers feel differently about the same passage. What is the best explanation?
choices: tone is chosen by each reader
mood can be influenced by readers’ experiences, while textual details still guide interpretation
